Figure 8-1 Ancillary systems in the exterior of the MTV Final Technical Report 34/57 Figure 8-2 Ancillary systems in the interior of the MTV (portside) Figure 8-3 Ancillary systems in the interior of the MTV (starboard) Final Technical Report 35/57 9 CONTROL SYSTEM DESIGN & INSTRUMENTATION The MTV will be equipped with a centralized control system with the main objective of enabling the configuration, control, and monitoring of the onboard systems while ensuring the safety of personnel and the MTV platform. To ensure maximum safety and reliability, the vessel will have three control systems: the Integrated Automation System (IAS), which will handle everyday vessel operations; the Data Acquisition System, and the Integrated Control System (ICS), which will oversee the rest of the systems of the vessel. The ICS control system and the IAS are the link to the subsystems (see Figure 9-1). More specifically, the vessel control system monitors and controls all navigation-related systems, as well as other pure- vessel systems such as the ballast & bilge and fire extinction systems. Additionally, other specific equipment that will not be commanded, and their data is not necessary to actuate in other systems, will be directly hard-wired to MODAQ, the data acquisition system (i.e., Weather Station, UPS data, etc.). Figure 9-1 Control system architecture The ICS control system directly oversees all the subsystems and equipment through the IAS. This closed and autonomous controller manages all the elements below and shares all the information from its equipment and subsystems with the ICS controller. The ICS software will be programmed using the IDOM Library, which is based on object-oriented programming and allows code reusability and easy maintenance. This software design comprises some controllers in charge of commanding all the systems and communicating between the three control systems mentioned before, as well as with any onshore station, enabling remote control of some systems in the MTV.
